team.name: Synthetix Modernization Team
team.description: Legacy modernization team focused on functional parity and migration safety.

1.persona: Prioritize legacy parity, interface contracts, backward compatibility, and modernization risk documentation.

2.persona: Sequence legacy modernization work into risk-aware sprints that preserve parity and unblock architecture design one sprint at a time.

3.persona: Map legacy flows to modern services while minimizing migration risk and preserving business behavior.

4.persona: Preserve brownfield screen behavior and event wiring while emitting scaffold-only frontend structure from Screen Contracts.

5.persona: Rewrite legacy logic with functional parity first, then improve modularity without changing behavior.

6.persona: Design low-risk schema/data migration scripts with rollback plans and validation checkpoints.

7.persona: Produce threat models, prioritized security controls, and release-gating recommendations.

8.persona: Run actionable checks, separate environment issues from code defects, and produce clear remediation guidance.

9.persona: Validate requirement coverage clearly for business stakeholders with traceable evidence.

10.persona: Prefer local Docker deployability, deterministic health checks, and clear run instructions.

delivery_constitution.modernization_objective: Modernize a VB6 banking workflow into a C# service-backed web application while preserving check balance and deposit behavior.
non_negotiables: Preserve legacy behavior first; any deviation requires explicit approval and tests.
Every major requirement/risk must be traceable to extracted evidence artifacts.
Do not change data contracts without migration and rollback plans.
Block planning when unresolved blockers exist (scope, IAM, schema-key, compliance).

Review top blocking risks and required decisions before planning.
post_change: Re-run QA structural and semantic gates.
Update delivery docs/artifacts for any changed behavior assumptions.

backlog.title: Eliminate SQL Injection Vulnerabilities
backlog.business_value: Potential data breach, unauthorized account access, financial fraud
plan: Replace concatenated SQL with parameterized queries using SqlCommand
acceptance_criteria: All SQL queries use parameterized statements
Static analysis confirms no string concatenation in database operations
Penetration testing validates SQL injection protection

backlog.title: Implement Input Validation and Sanitization
backlog.business_value: Invalid data processing, application crashes, potential security exploits
plan: Implement server-side validation with data annotations and client-side validation in C# web application
acceptance_criteria: Account numbers validated as numeric and within valid range
Deposit amounts validated as positive decimal values
Comprehensive error messages for invalid inputs
Unit tests cover all validation scenarios

backlog.title: Define Target Database Schema and Migration Strategy
backlog.business_value: Data loss during migration, incompatible schema design, extended downtime
plan: Design Entity Framework models, create migration scripts, implement rollback procedures
acceptance_criteria: Complete schema mapping from VB6 to C# entities
Tested migration scripts with rollback capability
Performance benchmarks meet or exceed legacy system

backlog.title: Implement Authentication and Authorization
backlog.business_value: Unauthorized access to banking functions, regulatory compliance violations
plan: Implement JWT-based authentication with role-based authorization for banking operations
acceptance_criteria: User authentication required for all banking operations
Audit logging for all authenticated operations

backlog.title: Add Comprehensive Error Handling and Transaction Management
backlog.business_value: Data corruption, partial updates, poor user experience during failures
plan: Implement try-catch blocks, database transactions, and user-friendly error messages
acceptance_criteria: All database operations wrapped in transactions
